<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2deca80ebb108f1b">Do exact length or posterior thresholds activate RLCPR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlcpr">RLCPR: Rethinking Probability-Based Reinforcement Learning From Posterior Concentration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Minimum length must strictly exceed its threshold and posterior range must be strictly below its bound. Entropy CDF also uses strict less-than on ties. Handcrafted numbers test formulas, not RL gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Minimum length exactly at threshold is not penalized.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01458">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01458-rlcpr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2deca80ebb108f1b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:range-grpo" data-paper-title="Range-GRPO: Policy Optimization via Pairwise Relations among Reward Intervals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-range-grpo-b66c385f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a15f72e3b4bd2e6e">Why use reward intervals instead of point scores in Range-GRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arange-grpo">Range-GRPO: Policy Optimization via Pairwise Relations among Reward Intervals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yonsei University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A point hides judge uncertainty. Intervals identify pair orderings that can be justified and avoid treating tiny noise as preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Strongly overlapping score ranges need not produce a winner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01548">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01548-range-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a15f72e3b4bd2e6e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:range-grpo" data-paper-title="Range-GRPO: Policy Optimization via Pairwise Relations among Reward Intervals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-58d186d40a148b8d">Why not rank replies with overlapping reward intervals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arange-grpo">Range-GRPO: Policy Optimization via Pairwise Relations among Reward Intervals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yonsei University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Small point differences may be judge noise. Use determinate calibrated interval relations and aggregate relative group advantage without inventing directions. Degenerate intervals recover point rewards. The kernel is not judge calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not favor one broad overlapping interval merely because its center is higher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01548">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01548-range-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58d186d40a148b8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:range-grpo" data-paper-title="Range-GRPO: Policy Optimization via Pairwise Relations among Reward Intervals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e90be0ef0d21656e">How does treating overlap as uncertain differ from midpoint ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arange-grpo">Range-GRPO: Policy Optimization via Pairwise Relations among Reward Intervals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yonsei University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Midpoints always impose order even inside large uncertainty. Interval comparison discards dubious direction, at the cost of sparser supervision. It does not prove faster/better training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different midpoints with overlap needn&#x27;t imply a clear preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01548">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01548-range-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e90be0ef0d21656e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:range-grpo" data-paper-title="Range-GRPO: Policy Optimization via Pairwise Relations among Reward Intervals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-50dbc843fd89d3de">Does local Range-GRPO calibrate a conformal judge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arange-grpo">Range-GRPO: Policy Optimization via Pairwise Relations among Reward Intervals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yonsei University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It consumes intervals and tests comparisons and the point limit. Coverage needs real calibration data/judging. Degenerate intervals should recover the DR-GRPO limit, not arbitrary smoothing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A wide interval passing an interface test doesn&#x27;t establish coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01548">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01548-range-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-50dbc843fd89d3de">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gmc-grpo" data-paper-title="Asynchronous LLM Post-Training: Group-Mass Capping and Convergence Analysis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gmc-grpo-1030f809" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4530e4fc6872ebb5">Why cap total group importance mass in GMC-GRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agmc-grpo">Asynchronous LLM Post-Training: Group-Mass Capping and Convergence Analysis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Asynchronous stale policies can produce huge ratios. Apply one multiplier to the group to cap mass while preserving within-group proportions, unlike independent clipping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scale the whole inflated group instead of cutting only its largest member.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01896">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01896-gmc-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4530e4fc6872ebb5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gmc-grpo" data-paper-title="Asynchronous LLM Post-Training: Group-Mass Capping and Convergence Analysis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c6f729f6a888dc53">Why rescale an entire group instead of clipping trajectories one by one?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agmc-grpo">Asynchronous LLM Post-Training: Group-Mass Capping and Convergence Analysis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent clipping changes relative weights. A shared factor limits total ratio mass and retains relative contributions. Sampling and moment assumptions remain; a formula test is not an asynchronous training system.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Uniformly scale stale trajectories when total mass is too large; separate caps can flatten differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01896">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01896-gmc-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c6f729f6a888dc53">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gmc-grpo" data-paper-title="Asynchronous LLM Post-Training: Group-Mass Capping and Convergence Analysis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4eea76d90300a7b0">What does a group cap preserve that per-trajectory clipping may not?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agmc-grpo">Asynchronous LLM Post-Training: Group-Mass Capping and Convergence Analysis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Common scaling retains ratios between weights. Independent caps change them. Theory still requires conditions such as common second moments; it does not repair arbitrary staleness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clipping may make large and medium weights equal, while group scaling preserves their ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01896">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01896-gmc-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4eea76d90300a7b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gmc-grpo" data-paper-title="Asynchronous LLM Post-Training: Group-Mass Capping and Convergence Analysis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1610e7e0c7bb3600">How do GMC weights behave below the total cap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agmc-grpo">Asynchronous LLM Post-Training: Group-Mass Capping and Convergence Analysis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use multiplier one until total exceeds cap; then multiply by cap divided by sum. Check nonnegative weights and group boundaries. Local kernel does not measure asynchronous cluster throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not pool two prompts: a large weight in one should not scale the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01896">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01896-gmc-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1610e7e0c7bb3600">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rfpo" data-paper-title="Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rfpo-964b9a42" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-679b738a1f593837">Does RFPO reward-free mean no quality signal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arfpo">Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Luxembourg</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A calibrated frozen critic predicts prefix success instead of costly external terminal rewards. Supervision moves into the critic, whose reliability still matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unfinished solution can get a success estimate because of prior evaluation learning, not by knowing the answer from nothing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37119">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37119-rfpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-679b738a1f593837">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rfpo" data-paper-title="Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfcc645e9e1f5910">Why debias and binarize a frozen critic instead of maximizing its continuous score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arfpo">Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Luxembourg</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing stops parameter drift, not bias. Policies can exploit length or other shortcuts. Debias and binarize prefix success estimates while using the critic for baselines and unfinished forecasts. Reward-free reuses supervision rather than removes it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A length-biased critic is exploitable even when frozen.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37119">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37119-rfpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cfcc645e9e1f5910">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rfpo" data-paper-title="Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-17d352b39cff66da">What risk comes from sharing a critic for reward and baseline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arfpo">Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Luxembourg</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared bias can be exploited by the policy. Length debiasing and binarization limit shortcuts without ensuring attack resistance. Critic score itself isn&#x27;t evidence of capability gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the critic favors verbosity, the policy may simply lengthen responses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37119">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37119-rfpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-17d352b39cff66da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rfpo" data-paper-title="Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee0051c78752baa7">Why freeze the RFPO critic and distinguish unfinished forecasts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arfpo">Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Luxembourg</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing keeps the evaluation baseline stable. A forecast handles missing terminal outcomes, not verified success. Local debiasing, binary reward and GAE kernels do not train a long-reasoning model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high estimate on a truncated trace remains an estimate, not an answer labeled correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37119">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37119-rfpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee0051c78752baa7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:graft" data-paper-title="Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-graft-20b4d98a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bfafd4bf9c31e789">When does GRAFT borrow a peer group?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agraft">Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>When receiver candidates all fail and a peer group for the same prompt contains both success and failure. Only then is there transferable relative credit; it is not copying one answer from the best model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four receiver failures can use a peer group with both correct and incorrect replies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37868">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37868-graft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bfafd4bf9c31e789">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:graft" data-paper-title="Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a8a72e7c33e77d4">Why exchange full same-prompt peer groups instead of only a winning answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agraft">Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A receiver all-fail group lacks differentiation; the whole peer group preserves successes, failures and their relative credit. Cross-model/tokenizer mismatch needs sequence compatibility and token clipping. Do not mark borrowed data on-policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Give the receiver a peer&#x27;s complete group and credit rather than inserting a single gold answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37868">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37868-graft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a8a72e7c33e77d4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:graft" data-paper-title="Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-18fb1d6cc0e5ef2d">Why borrow a complete peer group rather than one success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agraft">Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It retains internal advantages. Adding only a positive changes the group distribution and credit baseline. Borrowed trajectories are not receiver on-policy data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep peer failures to preserve why peer successes have relative positive advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37868">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37868-graft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18fb1d6cc0e5ef2d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:graft" data-paper-title="Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a391696ae8153767">Why use average sequence likelihood for cross-tokenizer GRAFT compatibility?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agraft">Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token counts and boundaries differ, so use sequence-level compatibility then ratio clipping to bound updates. Track text rescoring, provenance and group advantages. This doesn&#x27;t make policies identical.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same sentence tokenized differently cannot be compared by subtracting probabilities position by position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37868">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37868-graft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a391696ae8153767">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tlm-dre" data-paper-title="Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tlm-dre-7ebc851d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6dd63a8240c91c1f">Why model turns rather than average all tokens in TLM-DRE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atlm-dre">Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Turns have different roles and lengths. Multiscale weighting preserves dialogue structure; token averaging may let long turns dominate. Actual credit depends on density ratios and feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short crucial tool choice should not be drowned out by a verbose explanation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16760">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16760-tlm-dre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6dd63a8240c91c1f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tlm-dre" data-paper-title="Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8bf40a276febca62">Why upweight low-confidence TLM-DRE turns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atlm-dre">Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Length-normalized reference logp proxies how well a turn is learned. Lower confidence receives greater scale, changing multi-turn density ratios and asymmetric pressure. Low likelihood does not mean wrong. Local diagnostics do not establish generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct a hesitant tool decision more strongly than a confident recap, while recognizing rare valid actions can be unlikely.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16760">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16760-tlm-dre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8bf40a276febca62">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tlm-dre" data-paper-title="Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2313a70c65e97e9f">How does asymmetric positive/negative density weighting differ from uniform weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atlm-dre">Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Positive and negative evidence reinforce and suppress differently. A common curve removes that design, but asymmetry still needs real multi-turn evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rewarding a correct action and suppressing a wrong continuation need not share weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16760">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16760-tlm-dre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2313a70c65e97e9f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tlm-dre" data-paper-title="Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f874be5c36b0fbe">Does the local TLM-DRE kernel demonstrate real multi-turn agent training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atlm-dre">Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It computes reference turn weights and asymmetric token updates without an agent environment. Retain turn memberships; concatenating into one turn changes the method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three tool turns collapsed into a string cannot test the original allocation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16760">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16760-tlm-dre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f874be5c36b0fbe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mad-rl" data-paper-title="MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mad-rl-6dafc52d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9537d417371ba926">Why target output classes rather than token entropy in MaD-RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amad-rl">MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Classes measure semantic result frequencies; token entropy measures surface uncertainty. Many wordings can yield one class. Combine empirical-to-target class mismatch with correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many phrasings recommending the same item category do not improve category coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31644">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.31644-mad-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9537d417371ba926">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mad-rl" data-paper-title="MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-83efe3e396c5af87">Why match output-class frequencies instead of just raising token entropy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amad-rl">MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Randomized words can collapse to the same decision. Map outputs to classes and reward empirical-to-target similarity plus correctness. Hold frequencies fixed per update; unsampled classes get no fictitious on-policy examples. Specify invalid-output treatment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Check decisions directly even when language appears diverse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31644">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.31644-mad-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83efe3e396c5af87">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mad-rl" data-paper-title="MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-293edb5053eb4a47">What tradeoff does distribution matching add beyond maximizing accuracy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amad-rl">MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accuracy can favor easy classes, while matching moves mass toward target frequencies. Report both: matching doesn&#x27;t guarantee correctness and high accuracy doesn&#x27;t guarantee target ratios.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Balanced classes can still include wrong replies in one category.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31644">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.31644-mad-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-293edb5053eb4a47">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mad-rl" data-paper-title="MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aabb50423710ae5d">Can invalid outputs be dropped from MaD-RL frequency denominators?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amad-rl">MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not arbitrarily; doing so changes empirical frequencies and rewards. Treat frequencies as fixed per update, smooth zero target probabilities explicitly, and do not invent gradients for unsampled categories. Local diagnostics aren&#x27;t full training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Dropping all unclassifiable samples can make remaining frequencies appear closer to target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31644">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.31644-mad-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aabb50423710ae5d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tasco" data-paper-title="Beyond Confidence: Stability-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tasco-a3638c7c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ae37dc4a87906c6">Does TASCO adapt backbone weights or a lightweight prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atasco">Beyond Confidence: Stability-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chongqing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freeze the backbone and optimize an added prefix, changing conditioning without retraining the model or selecting only by sampling. It uses unlabeled current-task signals, never test gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Update prefix vectors and reread probabilities while leaving model layers and answer labels untouched.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11393">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11393-tasco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6ae37dc4a87906c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tasco" data-paper-title="Beyond Confidence: Stability-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3bf3e360a7863e6c">Why check stability in addition to confidence during TASCO adaptation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atasco">Beyond Confidence: Stability-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chongqing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Confidence can reinforce wrong answers. Keep backbone fixed, tune a small prefix and penalize unstable predictions under neighborhood perturbations. Stability is unlabeled evidence, not a correctness oracle; no real local LM prefix training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If equivalent wording changes the answer, high original confidence alone is a poor signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11393">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11393-tasco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3bf3e360a7863e6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tasco" data-paper-title="Beyond Confidence: Stability-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7138500cadc224d7">How do TASCO prefix updates and best-of-N spend extra compute differently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atasco">Beyond Confidence: Stability-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chongqing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>TASCO optimizes conditioning before a frozen model predicts; best-of-N generates and selects more candidates. Compare optimizer forwards/backwards and generation, not just candidate count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several gradient steps and several independently generated answers are different workloads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11393">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11393-tasco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7138500cadc224d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tasco" data-paper-title="Beyond Confidence: Stability-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e74343bb7ff5725">Does the local TASCO stability penalty train an actual LM prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atasco">Beyond Confidence: Stability-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chongqing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It implements random neighborhood perturbation and a stability reference kernel without a frozen LM prefix path. Small-vector tests do not establish test-time gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Stable numeric features do not show a language model&#x27;s prefix was optimized on tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
