</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:probe-erpo" data-paper-title="Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-probe-erpo-6a0c336f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e457206d88014d8c">Why does Probe-ERPO use probes independent of final answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprobe-erpo">Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gold is unavailable during test-time adaptation. Using it would defeat unlabeled adaptation. PCR uses probe consistency to decide reinforcement vs negative constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Check agreement from intermediate states instead of matching to gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09135">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.09135-probe-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e457206d88014d8c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:probe-erpo" data-paper-title="Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-974ed0304580b614">Why use answer-independent probe consistency and not reinforce the majority at low agreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprobe-erpo">Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Self-labeling can repeat errors. Output-free probes estimate consistency; high/low branches differ. Low agreement constrains lower ranks while entropy preserves exploration. Consistency is not supervised correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Conflicting probes justify suppressing weak options without blindly rewarding the highest vote count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09135">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.09135-probe-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-974ed0304580b614">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:probe-erpo" data-paper-title="Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7354527fcaae28bd">Why aren&#x27;t high-PCR reinforcement and low-PCR negative ranking ordinary pseudo-labeling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprobe-erpo">Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Low consistency supplies no reliable positive, so constrain poor candidates rather than canonize the majority. High agreement is only a clue; entropy control and independent evaluation still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>When candidates conflict, avoid weak ones without declaring one correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09135">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.09135-probe-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7354527fcaae28bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:probe-erpo" data-paper-title="Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c98f34ea7d7c7dc">May Probe-ERPO&#x27;s negative rank mask read the answer key?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprobe-erpo">Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use allowed probes and candidate rankings only; gold appears in independent scoring. A fixed mask validates the update path, not real probe discrimination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fixture can specify which positions to suppress without teaching automatic error detection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09135">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.09135-probe-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c98f34ea7d7c7dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ttpo" data-paper-title="TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ttpo-67dfbe79" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b00787b0189ac51">Why train TTPO majority-agreeing and dissenting trajectories separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Attpo">TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The majority may be wrong, and dissent provides a different signal. Use self-distillation for agreement and grouped RL for disagreement rather than one unlabeled pseudo-target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A majority answer and an alternative path do not share the same imitation objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27448-ttpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9b00787b0189ac51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ttpo" data-paper-title="TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-69b2a4247c96ba4a">Why use different objectives for majority agreement and disagreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Attpo">TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Copying consensus can spread errors. Self-distill agreeing replies, apply group RL to dissent, and filter already converged positions and high-confidence errors. No gold or claim that votes are truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t delete the dissenting answer outright; handle it under the relevant objective and reliability filters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27448-ttpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-69b2a4247c96ba4a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ttpo" data-paper-title="TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-eaac62071a684a01">What safeguards does TTPO add instead of treating the majority answer as gold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Attpo">TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Asymmetric objectives filter converged tokens and confident errors. It recognizes that consensus is not truth; filter quality matters and consensus isn&#x27;t independent validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A group can confidently agree on the same wrong answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27448-ttpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eaac62071a684a01">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ttpo" data-paper-title="TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-04141004d61046ff">Does local TTPO perform real test-time sampling and Qwen updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Attpo">TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It tests branch objectives and token selection only. Fixed candidates are not real unlabeled adaptation. Keep gold hidden before branch assignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Supplying answers for formula checks does not mean the model generated them on benchmark prompts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27448-ttpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-04141004d61046ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlvr-fusion" data-paper-title="Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rlvr-fusion-9745b358" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1279a9ea40e51b64">What resources do Merge, Mix RL and MOPD reuse in RLVR Fusion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlvr-fusion">Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Merge reuses expert weight deltas; Mix RL reuses training data; MOPD distills from experts using data. Resource requirements differ, so averages cannot choose a route alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Without original training data, available routes differ even if expert weights are present.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27409">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27409-rlvr-fusion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1279a9ea40e51b64">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlvr-fusion" data-paper-title="Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a1eadf46dc7ae5e">Why are Merge, Mix RL and MOPD different fusion operations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlvr-fusion">Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Merge combines expert parameter increments, Mix RL trains on combined data, and MOPD uses expert guidance with data. Availability and budget determine feasible routes. Similar means or a probability-vector proxy do not establish lossless checkpoint fusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Experts alone permit discussing parameter merging; data without experts cannot run the same distillation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27409">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27409-rlvr-fusion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a1eadf46dc7ae5e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlvr-fusion" data-paper-title="Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ceb497193b26b2dc">Why doesn&#x27;t similar average performance imply per-domain equivalence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlvr-fusion">Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Averages can cancel larger task gaps. Compare target domains, available experts/data and compute, not only mean scores or similar formulas.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Better math and worse code can yield the same mean without meeting the same needs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27409">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27409-rlvr-fusion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ceb497193b26b2dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlvr-fusion" data-paper-title="Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f2cc44b2ba85f0a">Why define Merge task vectors relative to a common base?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlvr-fusion">Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Expert minus base must share parameter coordinates and reference. Different bases/layouts don&#x27;t express comparable deltas. Local candidate merging isn&#x27;t checkpoint merging.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Experts with different vocabularies or tensor layouts cannot simply average deltas.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27409">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27409-rlvr-fusion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f2cc44b2ba85f0a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grin" data-paper-title="From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-grin-1eaeb543" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-873baedb77750dde">Why inject a golden response only into GRIN failure groups?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrin">From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Merced</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All-fail groups lack positive contrast. Verified solutions supply direction; preserve more native exploration when the student succeeds. Gold is training supervision, not evaluation input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Add a verified answer only after all attempts fail, not to every prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.25243-grin/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-873baedb77750dde">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grin" data-paper-title="From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f5bf75743d70577">Why correct GRIN injection by the mixed distribution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrin">From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Merced</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An expert addition was not an unguided current-policy sample. Correct with the mixture denominator; reduce injection as capability improves and return to exploration. Gold must not appear in evaluation/deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn from an injected verified solution without logging it as a student exploration success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.25243-grin/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f5bf75743d70577">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grin" data-paper-title="From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5936dbb1a152686">How does mixture correction differ from treating the expert answer as a student sample?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrin">From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Merced</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sampling includes the injection source, so the denominator must represent the mixture. Calling it pure on-policy misweights it and hides external knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An inserted expert solution was not drawn solely from the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.25243-grin/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5936dbb1a152686">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grin" data-paper-title="From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8650e7c6e350f94">Why use q_mix rather than frozen reference in GRIN&#x27;s importance ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrin">From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Merced</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>q_mix describes actual sampling; reference anchors regularization. Track mixture origins/probabilities. The deterministic diagnostic does not reproduce the paper&#x27;s knowledge-acquisition data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An old reference is not interchangeable with the expert that generated a sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.25243-grin/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8650e7c6e350f94">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erpo" data-paper-title="Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-erpo-0cf15e52" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dcb7785d8df7472f">Why observe drift on the input side in ERPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerpo">Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Response regularization directly limits exploration. ERPO controls induced question-distribution shift with question likelihood weights and Query-KL, moving where regularization applies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Balance which questions receive learning pressure rather than forcing old answer wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.23311-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dcb7785d8df7472f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erpo" data-paper-title="Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-474029342d1961bb">How does question-side ERPO regularization differ from constraining replies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerpo">Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Answer KL limits output drift and exploration directly. ERPO weighs queries with reference likelihood and constrains induced question drift, changing update allocation across inputs. It isn&#x27;t a renamed answer KL; typicality does not verify real query modeling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reweight familiar questions that dominate training rather than constrain every answer to mimic the old model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.23311-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-474029342d1961bb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erpo" data-paper-title="Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6c1dd6350ae3b8d">Can Query-KL and Policy-KL be interchanged in ERPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerpo">Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. One constrains question distribution, the other conditional replies, with different gradient boundaries. Applying pressure to the answer scoring function isn&#x27;t input-only control.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Which question is sampled and how it is answered are different distributions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.23311-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6c1dd6350ae3b8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erpo" data-paper-title="Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-25993f182c79b72b">Why is local ERPO typicality only a query-likelihood proxy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerpo">Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Finite candidate features approximate input typicality to test flow and gradients, not natural-question LM likelihood. Use frozen reference weights, not weights inferred from test correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Typical feature frequency isn&#x27;t the probability of a complete Chinese question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.23311-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-25993f182c79b72b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gcpo" data-paper-title="GCPO: Diagnosing and Constraining Subspace Geometry in Rollout RL for LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gcpo-c679efe1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7473bf332d552ad">Why protect dominant pretrained singular spaces in GCPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agcpo">GCPO: Diagnosing and Constraining Subspace Geometry in Rollout RL for LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rollout update spikes in principal spaces may precede validation regressions. Restrict updates to bilateral orthogonal complements to avoid overwriting principal mappings. Correlation doesn&#x27;t forbid learning in all dominant directions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Add task behavior in remaining directions while preserving important input/output mappings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.11674-gcpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7473bf332d552ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gcpo" data-paper-title="GCPO: Diagnosing and Constraining Subspace Geometry in Rollout RL for LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b228873198b3173b">Why project low-rank updates onto both singular complements rather than penalize overlap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agcpo">GCPO: Diagnosing and Constraining Subspace Geometry in Rollout RL for LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Soft cost permits principal-space drift at sufficient reward. Hard bilateral projection excludes it, keeping both input and output directions outside frozen principal spaces. Vector diagnostics are not layered LoRA training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Every valid update must avoid protected directions, rather than merely pay a penalty for touching them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.11674-gcpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b228873198b3173b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gcpo" data-paper-title="GCPO: Diagnosing and Constraining Subspace Geometry in Rollout RL for LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-14dc24b93afc8e6b">How does hard orthogonality differ from a soft projection penalty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agcpo">GCPO: Diagnosing and Constraining Subspace Geometry in Rollout RL for LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hard constraints exclude violating updates. Soft penalties allow an optimizer to trade violations against task gains. A larger penalty doesn&#x27;t establish exact bilateral orthogonality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A soft update may briefly enter the principal space; hard projection removes that component every time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.11674-gcpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-14dc24b93afc8e6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gcpo" data-paper-title="GCPO: Diagnosing and Constraining Subspace Geometry in Rollout RL for LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5dff608003ae7cdb">Does local GCPO validate per-layer bilateral LoRA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agcpo">GCPO: Diagnosing and Constraining Subspace Geometry in Rollout RL for LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A vector policy restricts the leading right space of empirical update covariance as a proxy. The paper fixes left and right matrix projections; one-sided vector tests do not verify them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A parameter vector lacks two independent matrix axes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.11674-gcpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5dff608003ae7cdb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erils" data-paper-title="Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-erils-07f1d788" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d48d992843b46b3e">Why introduce external rollouts in ERILS diffusion RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerils">Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student exploration may lack coverage, while external policies offer different denoising trajectories. Track source and length; high external reward isn&#x27;t native reachability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Log an external model&#x27;s alternative denoising path as external.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.01717-erils/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d48d992843b46b3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erils" data-paper-title="Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-671320bb53b7dd5a">Why not normalize native and external rollouts together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerils">Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Differences in length and rewards can turn provenance into advantage, letting one source dominate. ERILS caps external lengths and treats reward sources separately. This preserves exploration value, not immunity to off-policy errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If outsiders are always longer and higher-scoring, pooled normalization may make every student sample negative.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.01717-erils/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-671320bb53b7dd5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erils" data-paper-title="Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8597a1ba52af3551">Why normalize sources separately rather than mix on/off-policy rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerils">Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sources can differ in reward scale and distribution; pooled baselines can systematically suppress one. Separate normalization preserves within-source credit without solving every off-policy bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A higher expert mean can make useful student improvements negative under one pooled baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.01717-erils/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8597a1ba52af3551">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erils" data-paper-title="Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f3e41502de5e0cd">Why explicitly enforce external response length in ERILS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerils">Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long trajectories consume tokens and change loss scale. Retain length constraints and source labels through normalization. Candidate-policy diagnostics do not reproduce diffusion checkpoint training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An oversized expert trajectory could consume the batch and change the intended mixture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.01717-erils/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f3e41502de5e0cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:reco-grpo" data-paper-title="ReCo" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-reco-grpo-97f782ad" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c34e2c8ac9baa559">Why does ReCo address both duplicate replies and saturated tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Areco-grpo">ReCo</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Common responses dominate sample weight and already-certain tokens can be reinforced repeatedly. Expected response counts and token variance ratios target different redundancies to retain exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeated solutions and their nearly certain format tokens can both dominate gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26862">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.26862-reco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c34e2c8ac9baa559">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:reco-grpo" data-paper-title="ReCo" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-24eff40b49e92f55">Why downweight common replies and adjust individual-token variance separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Areco-grpo">ReCo</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Response weights correct expected repetition across the group; token variance measures local plasticity. Neither replaces the other. Coverage isn&#x27;t arbitrary randomness; candidate probabilities do not show long-text coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Downweighting repeated template responses can still leave nearly deterministic final tokens dominating.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26862">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.26862-reco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24eff40b49e92f55">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:reco-grpo" data-paper-title="ReCo" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-44a200aee7cb27b3">Is deduplication equivalent to ReCo expected-count weighting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Areco-grpo">ReCo</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hard dedup drops repeated samples; expected-count weights vary continuously with policy likelihood. A separate variance ratio adjusts tokens. The objectives differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two responses may appear only once each while one has much higher underlying probability and different weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26862">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.26862-reco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44a200aee7cb27b3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:reco-grpo" data-paper-title="ReCo" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7324658a6699d93">Why preserve old versus current probability in ReCo&#x27;s Bernoulli variance ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Areco-grpo">ReCo</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare current p(1−p) to old variance for changes in decision saturation. Protect near-zero denominators, not use current on both sides and get one. Candidate tests aren&#x27;t text pass@64.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Check numerical stability when old probability is near a boundary instead of accepting an enormous anomalous signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26862">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.26862-reco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7324658a6699d93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:code-optimization-rl" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-code-optimization-rl-602974e9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c4471ecbedbb6a3">Why isn&#x27;t correctness alone enough for code optimization RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acode-optimization-rl">Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The task also targets speed, but input size and load affect timing. Use dedicated tests and calibration to separate actual improvements from noise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two correct algorithms may show complexity differences only at larger inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.25970-code-optimization-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c4471ecbedbb6a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:code-optimization-rl" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2d56a2f3fb13d993">Why calibrate timing before rewarding speed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acode-optimization-rl">Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Noise from workers and small tests can teach exploitation rather than optimization. Independent timing, correctness and performance tests define valid rewards, with sparse/stale handling afterward. Syntax/fixtures don&#x27;t prove faster production.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeat timing under matched conditions instead of rewarding a run that happened on an idle host.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.25970-code-optimization-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2d56a2f3fb13d993">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:code-optimization-rl" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4891bbeecea8b14a">How does runtime reward differ from a math verifier?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acode-optimization-rl">Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correctness can be relatively deterministic; time depends on inputs, sandbox and load. Use gates and reference percentiles, not one wall-clock observation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A busy shared worker can slow unchanged code without a regression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.25970-code-optimization-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4891bbeecea8b14a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:code-optimization-rl" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0b6f1cfd3a1e5ab">Can the local code-optimization component replace a timing service?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acode-optimization-rl">Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Real rewards need correctness and optimization tests, independent sandbox calibration, and handling sparse advantages and stale batches. A reward formula is not execution or acceleration evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Synthetic speed scores test update plumbing without timing code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:off-context-grpo" data-paper-title="Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-off-context-grpo-ccd1608e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-71690cceadeeaf26">Why let only Off-Context GRPO behavior see privileged hints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoff-context-grpo">Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hints help collect successes while the target sees the original prompt as deployed. Letting target see the solution evidence would change the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sampler can see a draft; omit it when scoring the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19313">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.19313-off-context-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-71690cceadeeaf26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:off-context-grpo" data-paper-title="Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a3ebe3e47f8ed51">Why sample with hints but optimize and infer without them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoff-context-grpo">Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hints increase successful trajectories and shift behavior. Correct using unhinted target versus hinted behavior ratio. Dropping denominator or retaining hints at evaluation changes the claimed task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A training draft can help collect a solution; the student and test still see only the problem.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19313">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.19313-off-context-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a3ebe3e47f8ed51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:off-context-grpo" data-paper-title="Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1b49e62f44a966b7">How does Off-Context GRPO differ from SFT on hinted replies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoff-context-grpo">Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It retains verifiable rewards and relative group signals and corrects hinted behavior versus unhinted target. Imitation doesn&#x27;t automatically correct that shift. Both must isolate evaluation gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A hint makes a path common without implying the unhinted model originally sampled it often.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19313">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.19313-off-context-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1b49e62f44a966b7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:off-context-grpo" data-paper-title="Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4a13b9d97f85b98">What contexts condition numerator and denominator in Off-Context GRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoff-context-grpo">Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Numerator uses target probability on the original prompt; denominator uses actual behavior probability with privileged context. Same reply prefix, different contexts; don&#x27;t add the hint to both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Strip hints only from target scoring, not from the sampled behavior&#x27;s probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19313">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.19313-off-context-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4a13b9d97f85b98">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:iso-rlvr" data-paper-title="ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-iso-rlvr-42a6dc22" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f42c411f56be25bc">Why freeze singular values but adjust singular frames in ISO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aiso-rlvr">ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed spectral strength and rotated input/output directions constrain adaptation without freezing the whole layer or keeping function unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same stretches in rotated bases can act on different features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.19331-iso-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f42c411f56be25bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:iso-rlvr" data-paper-title="ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d6e53e6e465caeee">How does fixed-spectrum ISO differ from ordinary low-rank updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aiso-rlvr">ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It adjusts input/output singular directions while retaining magnitudes, rather than adding arbitrary low-rank changes. This constrains reachable weights and structures expert merges. Small tests don&#x27;t establish full model optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal singular values with rotated directions can implement different mappings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.19331-iso-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d6e53e6e465caeee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:iso-rlvr" data-paper-title="ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6056b798db106b9">Are ISO fixed spectrum and GCPO protected subspaces the same?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aiso-rlvr">ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. ISO fixes values and changes frames; GCPO excludes updates into selected principal directions. They fix different quantities and allow different changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rotating directions at fixed scale isn&#x27;t holding principal directions fixed and using their complement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.19331-iso-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6056b798db106b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:iso-rlvr" data-paper-title="ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f88d7e0f9daefca">How avoid training Σ in ISO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aiso-rlvr">ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep Σ0 fixed and optimize only permitted input/output frames, checking structure. Free matrix updates change spectrum. Local candidate tests don&#x27;t cover the full LLM stack.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Unrestricted gradients on a reconstructed weight bypass fixed singular values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.19331-iso-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f88d7e0f9daefca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ripo" data-paper-title="RIPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ripo-458e77e0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c4c25eef9c2cb71">Why does a fixed ratio clip give uneven distance budgets in RIPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aripo">RIPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal ratio changes have different geometric effects at different old probabilities. Fisher–Rao geometry adjusts bounds for more comparable local budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same relative increase for rare and frequent actions need not move the distribution equally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10169">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.10169-ripo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6c4c25eef9c2cb71">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
