<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ripo" data-paper-title="RIPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-925d5b7d5f114e23">Why isn&#x27;t one PPO ratio interval the same policy distance at every old probability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aripo">RIPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local geometry and KL cost depend on old probability. RIPO uses Fisher–Rao probability-dependent bounds, not different advantage labels. Actual update stability still needs verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Doubling rare and common actions affects remaining mass differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10169">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.10169-ripo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-925d5b7d5f114e23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ripo" data-paper-title="RIPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-733379e1b83a5724">How do adaptive RIPO bounds differ from raising global PPO ε?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aripo">RIPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global ε broadens every action. RIPO conditions bounds on old probability rather than uniformly becoming more aggressive, without guaranteeing universal stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Exploration needs in low-probability regions need not relax frequent actions equally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10169">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.10169-ripo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-733379e1b83a5724">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ripo" data-paper-title="RIPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-68231f74e75567f7">Should RIPO dynamic clipping read pre- or post-update probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aripo">RIPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Set boundaries from frozen old-policy action probabilities while evaluating current ratios. Recomputing from current shifts the trust region during updates. Candidate tests aren&#x27;t long-CoT training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Increasing an action&#x27;s probability should not rewrite that round&#x27;s original bound.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10169">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.10169-ripo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-68231f74e75567f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sis" data-paper-title="Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sis-7add6071" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-032fce07199c0994">Why convert some old-policy SIS tokens into usable current-policy samples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asis">Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Asynchrony/reuse induce staleness and products of ratios have high variance. Rejection sampling reduces correction for accepted tokens; the host method handles rejected ones without dropping all data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retain useful accepted positions within an old batch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04728">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.04728-sis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-032fce07199c0994">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sis" data-paper-title="Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1196d9cfe453f499">Why does SIS set accepted ratios to one, and does this make the whole trajectory on-policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asis">Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Under ideal rejection sampling the accepted conditional action distribution is corrected at a fixed prefix, so no original ratio is needed there. Rejects follow host correction. Whole histories remain old, and top-K is approximate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Accepting one position never sets all trajectory ratios to one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04728">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.04728-sis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1196d9cfe453f499">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sis" data-paper-title="Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-81cc7a58bc1c0e36">Is setting accepted token ratios to one the same as clipping to one?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asis">Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Acceptance is a distributional rejection-sampling event, not numerical capping. Exact envelopes and behavior top-K approximations have different guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Replacing every large ratio with one gives no sampling guarantee.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04728">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.04728-sis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-81cc7a58bc1c0e36">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sis" data-paper-title="Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1eeece4be8b6c955">Which policy supplies SIS top-K, and what happens to rejections?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asis">Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Approximate the envelope on behavior top-K. Set accepted ratios to one, keep GRPO/DAPO/GSPO correction for rejected tokens, rather than deleting or resetting them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One rejected token does not force dropping the full reply.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04728">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.04728-sis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1eeece4be8b6c955">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stare" data-paper-title="STARE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-stare-ca64b168" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cf2187d20e32967c">Why focus STARE on surprising tokens rather than equally reinforce a trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astare">STARE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same advantage can affect entropy differently by position. Select critical surprisal quantiles and adjust weights with target-entropy feedback, not terminal reward alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An uncertain branch and punctuation can share reward without serving equal exploration roles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.19236-stare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cf2187d20e32967c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stare" data-paper-title="STARE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-faaef258a6b76c26">Why combine surprisal with target entropy rather than always reward surprising tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astare">STARE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Surprising positions can influence entropy strongly; amplifying them always can overdisperse policy. Select batch quantiles, then adjust advantages based on entropy error. Surprise is not a correct-action label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare token can need opposite adjustments under an overconfident vs overrandom policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.19236-stare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-faaef258a6b76c26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stare" data-paper-title="STARE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc56eb8e87c7dbc1">How does STARE&#x27;s entropy feedback differ from a fixed entropy bonus?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astare">STARE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed bonuses always push one direction; feedback reacts to the current–target gap. Targets and measurement matter. Higher entropy is not inherently better and surprise doesn&#x27;t imply correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Above-target entropy requires a different control direction from below-target entropy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.19236-stare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc56eb8e87c7dbc1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stare" data-paper-title="STARE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-144b8b66263c2dbb">Why identify STARE positions by batch quantiles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astare">STARE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Quantiles measure relative salience in the current batch, not an absolute threshold. Fix valid-token masks and probability source; exclude padding. Local checks cover weighting and feedback only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Artificial low padding probabilities can shift the critical quantile.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.19236-stare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-144b8b66263c2dbb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:kpop" data-paper-title="KPop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-kpop-03b1bc3e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c555e547d25d78c">Why represent one token and the remaining vocabulary as binary in KPop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Akpop">KPop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ling / Ring Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A sampled ratio ignores absolute mass. Binary comparison includes both token and complement, using forward/reverse KL to gate train–serve mismatch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal multiplicative changes for rare and common tokens affect complement mass differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15079">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.15079-kpop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c555e547d25d78c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:kpop" data-paper-title="KPop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d03b1e6d172879e3">Why compare both binary KLs rather than only bound a ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Akpop">KPop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ling / Ring Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same ratio means different movement at different token probabilities. The binary distribution captures token and complement, and KL asymmetry motivates both directions. Passing does not establish token correctness or system-wide lack of bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same relative shift for a rare and common word is not geometrically equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15079">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.15079-kpop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d03b1e6d172879e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:kpop" data-paper-title="KPop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bbe37f3bfe81534">How does bidirectional binary KL differ from a fixed ratio mask?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Akpop">KPop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ling / Ring Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KL depends on probability level, whereas a ratio mask uses relative multiples. Both directions must pass because KL is asymmetric. A mask doesn&#x27;t validate synchronization of real asynchronous serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small KL one way can hide mismatch the other way.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15079">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.15079-kpop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bbe37f3bfe81534">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:kpop" data-paper-title="KPop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b948a36fbc87ae40">Does KPop retain a token if either KL is small or only if both are?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Akpop">KPop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ling / Ring Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both directions must be at or below threshold. Stabilize boundary probabilities and track serving vs training source. No local real train/inference engine or MoE cluster.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Passing only train-to-serve KL still means mask out.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15079">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.15079-kpop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b948a36fbc87ae40">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gprl" data-paper-title="GPRL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gprl-3009fd16" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-fcd8ef0ba525dcfd">Why compute GPRL group advantages per preference dimension?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agprl">GPRL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dimensions have different units and variance. Normalize separately, then aggregate by task context. Normalization avoids accidental numerical dominance, not a claim of equal importance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 100-point format scale would swamp binary correctness under raw summation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18721">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.18721-gprl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fcd8ef0ba525dcfd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gprl" data-paper-title="GPRL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d36e96fff938a5a3">Why normalize GPRL advantages by dimension before context aggregation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agprl">GPRL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw sums let large scales or variance dominate and hide tradeoffs among helpfulness, format and brevity. Standardize, weight by context and monitor drift. Normalization isn&#x27;t value prioritization; exact accuracy isn&#x27;t a multi-dimensional evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Separate a 100-point metric&#x27;s units from how much users want it weighted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18721">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.18721-gprl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d36e96fff938a5a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gprl" data-paper-title="GPRL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4acbb9a1f4e30016">How does GPRL differ from summing rewards then applying GRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agprl">GPRL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summation mixes scales and conflicts before normalization. Separate standardization preserves each dimension&#x27;s relative information before aggregation; the operations do not commute. Test context weights and drift separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One high-variance dimension can dominate normalized totals while others barely matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18721">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.18721-gprl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4acbb9a1f4e30016">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gprl" data-paper-title="GPRL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f517255fce38ba7b">Does local GPRL exact-answer regression refute the paper&#x27;s open-ended results?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agprl">GPRL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Retain the negative accuracy result, but real human multi-dimensional preferences and open generation judging are absent. Track per-dimension mean, variance and effective weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Brevity can improve while exact match worsens, so answer score alone isn&#x27;t complete.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18721">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.18721-gprl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f517255fce38ba7b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:conspo" data-paper-title="ConSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-conspo-ff3e363d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e9fd63f5b835a51b">Why use group InfoNCE for sequence preference in ConSPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconspo">ConSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiple same-prompt sequences compete in one objective. Average logp reduces length scale effects and temperature controls separation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Boost a good solution relative to alternatives rather than score its likelihood alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.12969-conspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e9fd63f5b835a51b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:conspo" data-paper-title="ConSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dcba0d92e323eff2">Why use length-normalized sequence scores for InfoNCE rather than cumulative token reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconspo">ConSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summed logp changes scale with length and can confuse verbosity with quality. Average per response then contrast within the same prompt. Temperature and normalization still affect gradients; relative quality is not absolute correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two correct replies can differ in length; average before comparing so raw sum does not penalize the longer one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.12969-conspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dcba0d92e323eff2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:conspo" data-paper-title="ConSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c52cad0e9bc58eaf">How does ConSPO group contrast differ from independent binary pairs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconspo">ConSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One denominator couples all candidates, unlike independent pair losses. Group size and negative composition change the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new competitor changes the shared denominator, not just one pair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.12969-conspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c52cad0e9bc58eaf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:conspo" data-paper-title="ConSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6584c823e36000c0">Where do length normalization and temperature apply in ConSPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconspo">ConSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Average valid-response logp, divide by temperature, then use stable group log-sum-exp. Exclude prompts/padding. Local kernel is not paper-scale training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing tokenwise temperature and denominator arbitrarily departs from sequence scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.12969-conspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6584c823e36000c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:missing-old-logits" data-paper-title="Missing Old Logits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-missing-old-logits-37bc553d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-09973dbae7619570">Why is Missing Old Logits more than a logging issue?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amissing-old-logits">Missing Old Logits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Historical training-side probabilities separate train–inference mismatch from stale weights. Serving probabilities alone conflate both, making the correction ambiguous.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Token drift can come from engine differences or several policy updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.12070-missing-old-logits/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-09973dbae7619570">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:missing-old-logits" data-paper-title="Missing Old Logits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-460fc794c3daf6c8">Why can&#x27;t the total ratio disentangle mismatch and staleness without old training logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amissing-old-logits">Missing Old Logits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Current training vs old inference factors through old training probabilities. Missing that intermediate hides whether changes come from the engine or updates. Recover the anchor by snapshot or an old-logit model, not zero-fill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A changed score on an old sample cannot identify the original engine gap without its training snapshot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.12070-missing-old-logits/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-460fc794c3daf6c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:missing-old-logits" data-paper-title="Missing Old Logits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-da5bb471e20b2a8f">Why do train–inference and staleness corrections need different denominators?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amissing-old-logits">Missing Old Logits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One compares training and serving implementations of the same old policy; the other compares current and old training policies. Their product is the total ratio, not interchangeable terms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing inference engines at fixed weights can create mismatch without training staleness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.12070-missing-old-logits/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da5bb471e20b2a8f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:missing-old-logits" data-paper-title="Missing Old Logits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-19100a5769e4bc47">Can current logits simply replace missing old training logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amissing-old-logits">Missing Old Logits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Snapshots, old-logit models, interrupted synchronization and EWMA are explicit alternatives with costs/assumptions. Local decomposition and state tests are not cluster deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rescoring old samples with updated weights rewrites the baseline rather than restoring history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.12070-missing-old-logits/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-19100a5769e4bc47">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:luspo" data-paper-title="LUSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-luspo-8b4b98a1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e5434f9738f469e">Why examine response-length trajectories in LUSPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aluspo">LUSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>RLVR objectives implicitly weight length differently, potentially causing collapse or drift. Normalize sequence logp as prescribed to separate reward learning from length scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Stable accuracy with shrinking replies can still lose long-reasoning coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2602.05261-luspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e5434f9738f469e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:luspo" data-paper-title="LUSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-335bdae0fb18cc4d">Why can sequence-level LUSPO updates still need length-bias checks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aluspo">LUSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Aggregation does not remove length coupling in cumulative logp. LUSPO reorganizes scores to avoid systematic length pressure. Short-task normalization checks do not validate long-CoT dynamics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two replies with similar per-token changes can have different cumulative ratios solely because of length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2602.05261-luspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-335bdae0fb18cc4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:luspo" data-paper-title="LUSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-76dd1146a3249f22">How does the LUSPO sequence ratio differ from tokenwise clipping?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aluspo">LUSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exponentiate length-normalized sequence log-ratio and share the signal over the response. Tokenwise clips act locally, with different dynamics. Sequence aggregation alone doesn&#x27;t guarantee long-length stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An increased token ratio and a decreased one can cancel in a sequence but clip differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2602.05261-luspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-76dd1146a3249f22">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:luspo" data-paper-title="LUSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d27849877ca4fb1">Why don&#x27;t local short arithmetic tasks establish long-CoT length stability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aluspo">LUSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generation, sequence ratios and normalization run, but short replies do not cover long reasoning dynamics. Use effective response length without padding/prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A dozen-word answer doesn&#x27;t test drift across thousands of tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2602.05261-luspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d27849877ca4fb1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:calibration-aware-rl" data-paper-title="Balancing Classification and Calibration Performance in Decision-Making LLMs via Calibration Aware Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-calibration-aware-rl-6e3cb1f1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b4f067719b7ff0b1">Does calibration-aware RL score the entire explanation through its decision token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acalibration-aware-rl">Balancing Classification and Calibration Performance in Decision-Making LLMs via Calibration Aware Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It studies final-decision probability and calibration, not factual fidelity of all reasoning. Correct choices and credible probabilities require separate measurement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>High probability for A doesn&#x27;t make every preceding explanation step correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13284">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2601.13284-calibration-aware-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b4f067719b7ff0b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:calibration-aware-rl" data-paper-title="Balancing Classification and Calibration Performance in Decision-Making LLMs via Calibration Aware Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c73529324e3dd75">Why constrain decision probability if accuracy improves while ECE worsens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acalibration-aware-rl">Balancing Classification and Calibration Performance in Decision-Making LLMs via Calibration Aware Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correctness only needs the top class right; calibration requires confidence to match actual hit frequency. RLVR can make correct choices overconfident. Measure separately, choose T on validation and reserve test. Post-hoc calibration is not full RL reproduction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two models with identical labels can assign near-certainty or moderate confidence and differ in probability quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13284">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2601.13284-calibration-aware-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c73529324e3dd75">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:calibration-aware-rl" data-paper-title="Balancing Classification and Calibration Performance in Decision-Making LLMs via Calibration Aware Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e7311780075723f">How does local temperature calibration differ from full RLVR training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acalibration-aware-rl">Balancing Classification and Calibration Performance in Decision-Making LLMs via Calibration Aware Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Temperature rescales existing logits; full training changes the decision model. Shared calibration goals do not make postprocessing a full reproduction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A frozen model with tuned T uses no resampled trajectories or policy gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13284">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2601.13284-calibration-aware-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e7311780075723f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:calibration-aware-rl" data-paper-title="Balancing Classification and Calibration Performance in Decision-Making LLMs via Calibration Aware Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-586428ee262c0ee4">May calibration T be selected on test NLL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acalibration-aware-rl">Balancing Classification and Calibration Performance in Decision-Making LLMs via Calibration Aware Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fit validation NLL, freeze, then report test accuracy and calibration. Choosing on test biases final evaluation. Local coverage is calibration and split isolation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Trying all temperatures on test and reporting the best overstates generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13284">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2601.13284-calibration-aware-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-586428ee262c0ee4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:online-icepop" data-paper-title="Online IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-online-icepop-2e9d86d8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-491d6e763ccc16dc">Why consume each Online IcePop rollout batch once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aonline-icepop">Online IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One update avoids extra staleness from reuse, making initial policy ratio one. Train/inference numerical correction remains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Discard the fresh batch after its update instead of optimizing against it again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/1984379979035850499">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/web-2025-online-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-491d6e763ccc16dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:online-icepop" data-paper-title="Online IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d8fc111dd88f837">Why retain engine correction when Online IcePop updates only once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aonline-icepop">Online IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fresh one-use rollouts eliminate reuse staleness, so policy ratio at sampling is one and PPO clipping unnecessary. Equal weights can still produce different probabilities in training vs inference; IcePop keeps its two-sided mask and in-range ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fresh answer can come from a lower-precision engine; freshness is not engine equality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/1984379979035850499">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/web-2025-online-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d8fc111dd88f837">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:online-icepop" data-paper-title="Online IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-16114b522aa61dbb">Which correction does Online IcePop remove?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aonline-icepop">Online IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Remove reuse-induced stale-policy ratio and PPO clip, not the two-sided engine mask or original in-range ratio. Repeated updates invalidate the online simplification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scheduling must enforce one use; deleting a line doesn&#x27;t make training online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/1984379979035850499">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/web-2025-online-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16114b522aa61dbb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:online-icepop" data-paper-title="Online IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c2fc001681f837ad">How verify Online IcePop never silently reuses a batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aonline-icepop">Online IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Track unique batch IDs and consumption; reject a second update. A local candidate group is only a scheduling proxy, not distributed rollout infrastructure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retried delivery of the same batch is not fresh data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/1984379979035850499">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/web-2025-online-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c2fc001681f837ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minirl" data-paper-title="Stabilizing RL with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-minirl-5767c2fc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-fe81c4815abf4b1f">Why model both train/inference mismatch and staleness in miniRL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminirl">Stabilizing RL with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Qwen Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal weights may score differently across engines; old/new weights drift through learning. Separate them for appropriate on/off-policy correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A kernel change and a policy update are distinct causes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01374">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2512.01374-minirl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fe81c4815abf4b1f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minirl" data-paper-title="Stabilizing RL with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a451194042251330">Why split engine mismatch and policy staleness, and where does routing replay help?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminirl">Stabilizing RL with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Qwen Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Numerical engine differences and weight drift are distinct. Correct on-policy probabilities, combine off-policy updates with clipping and replay rollout MoE routing to reduce path mismatch. Both probabilities and paths need testing; local kernels aren&#x27;t a cluster.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One token may route to different experts even with synchronized weights, which a stale-policy ratio does not fix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01374">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2512.01374-minirl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a451194042251330">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minirl" data-paper-title="Stabilizing RL with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1ec329e91d3f23e">What do MoE Routing Replay and ratio clipping address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminirl">Stabilizing RL with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Qwen Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replay restores expert execution paths; clipping limits update magnitude from probabilities. Clipping cannot reconstruct old routes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Saving which expert executed is different from lowering a large ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01374">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2512.01374-minirl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1ec329e91d3f23e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minirl" data-paper-title="Stabilizing RL with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b23a91234d3e2e2">Does the local miniRL kernel prove distributed MoE stability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminirl">Stabilizing RL with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Qwen Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks correction, clipping and routing state semantics. Real replay needs recorded token routes and actual aligned execution, not a label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A replay flag doesn&#x27;t prove forward passes used the recorded experts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01374">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2512.01374-minirl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b23a91234d3e2e2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:icepop" data-paper-title="IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-icepop-96432a79" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-72e55a56d06c1046">Why does IcePop mask very small train-to-serve ratios?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aicepop">IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Upper clipping only controls huge weights; tiny ratios may also signal mismatch. A two-sided interval keeps trustworthy ratios without snapping others to boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A training probability far below serving can be unreliable even though its weight is small.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72e55a56d06c1046">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:icepop" data-paper-title="IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6dd13d3913684d0d">How is zeroing out-of-range IcePop updates different from clipping to a boundary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aicepop">IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clipping preserves boundary-weighted contribution; masking drops the current token gradient. IcePop uses two fixed bounds and original in-range correction. It filters mismatch, not text quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tiny ratio is unaffected by upper clipping, but two-sided masking excludes it instead of raising it to the lower bound.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6dd13d3913684d0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:icepop" data-paper-title="IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8939bfededdaa33b">How do IcePop masking and TIS clipping treat out-of-range samples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aicepop">IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>IcePop zeroes their gradient; TIS caps high weights but keeps them contributing. IcePop uses original in-range ratios, not ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An oversized ratio can retain capped contribution in TIS but none in IcePop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8939bfededdaa33b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:icepop" data-paper-title="IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ebbae817f487cec">Must IcePop distinguish engine ratio from policy ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aicepop">IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Engine ratio measures implementation mismatch; policy ratio measures current vs sampling policy. Mask the specified engine ratio only. No local real MoE/asynchronous system.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Using model-learning drift as the engine mask could drop normal probability changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ebbae817f487cec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gppo" data-paper-title="GPPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gppo-ce7f50e5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7a918e89b2d7d6b">Which PPO gradients does GPPO recover?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agppo">GPPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordinary clipping can stop gradients for positive-advantage high ratios and negative-advantage low ratios. GPPO restores backward signal while keeping the forward value.</p>
