<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A bad action already made rarer may still need an avoidance gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2508.07629-gppo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7a918e89b2d7d6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gppo" data-paper-title="GPPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7ded4f2a343eef5f">Why can GPPO have PPO-like forward values and nonzero clipped-region gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agppo">GPPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stop-gradient constructions decouple clipping values and derivatives. Boundary weights restore learning in flattened quadrants for positive exploration and negative examples. Inspect gradients, not just loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two operators can print one clipped score but only one has a boundary-weighted derivative.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2508.07629-gppo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7ded4f2a343eef5f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gppo" data-paper-title="GPPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0106d720dd6e5fbf">Why can identical forward losses produce different updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agppo">GPPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stop-gradient can change derivatives without changing values. GPPO separates forward and backward, so scalar logs cannot verify it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two functions with equal output can have different derivatives through detach.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2508.07629-gppo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0106d720dd6e5fbf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gppo" data-paper-title="GPPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e05efa68db424685">Is equality of clipped GPPO/PPO loss values enough to test implementation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agppo">GPPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Verify gradients in out-of-bound advantage quadrants against PPO&#x27;s zero gradients, and explicit detach boundaries. No paper-scale long-CoT training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Positive advantage and a ratio above the upper bound directly test the recovered path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2508.07629-gppo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e05efa68db424685">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tis" data-paper-title="TIS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tis-834fa80d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-af8f5cde5a29c025">Why use TIS for equal-weight training and inference engines?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atis">TIS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Precision and kernels can change probabilities, so rollout and training rescoring distributions differ. The ratio corrects implementation mismatch, not task rewards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two compute paths using identical weights can assign slightly different token likelihoods.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://fengyao.notion.site/off-policy-rl">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-af8f5cde5a29c025">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tis" data-paper-title="TIS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-741f3036cd257055">Why upper-clip engine ratios but keep small weights in TIS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atis">TIS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correction targets the training distribution. Huge weights can dominate variance; cap them. Small ratios indicate smaller target contributions, not automatic invalidity. This is not PPO policy ratio or two-sided masking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A token common in rollout but rare in training should contribute less without necessarily being removed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://fengyao.notion.site/off-policy-rl">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-741f3036cd257055">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tis" data-paper-title="TIS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-444934d9fbc8e69e">Why does TIS upper-clip instead of two-sided dropping like IcePop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atis">TIS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Capping large weights controls heavy tails while retaining small contributions. Two-sided masking drops severe mismatch in either direction. Zeroing small TIS weights changes the method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tiny TIS ratio still contributes a little.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://fengyao.notion.site/off-policy-rl">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-444934d9fbc8e69e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tis" data-paper-title="TIS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6194fab57efb0811">Which probability is the TIS denominator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atis">TIS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the actual rollout engine probability below corresponding training probability; a separate policy ratio may follow. Local deterministic perturbations aren&#x27;t vLLM/FSDP validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reversing the ratio can upweight an example that should be downweighted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://fengyao.notion.site/off-policy-rl">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6194fab57efb0811">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gspo" data-paper-title="GSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gspo-8ccc0734" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b426bfd8e95bfd5">Why use one importance ratio for a full response in GSPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agspo">GSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Qwen Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal reward is sequence-level, and token outliers can cause fragmented clipping. Average token log ratios to form one response weight and avoid local outlier dominance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One rare token&#x27;s large shift need not determine distinct clips throughout a long reply.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18071">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b426bfd8e95bfd5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gspo" data-paper-title="GSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b968145af51dfe73">Why average token log ratios before exponentiation and clipping?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agspo">GSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Qwen Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One outcome belongs to one answer. One geometric weight gives all tokens the same relative advantage and clipping decision despite local noise. It changes credit aggregation and doesn&#x27;t eliminate all length/MoE mismatches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct answer with one anomalous ratio gets different credit under token clipping and shared weighting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18071">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b968145af51dfe73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gspo" data-paper-title="GSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d23ce2ac81343580">Is GSPO&#x27;s geometric-mean ratio the actual sequence probability ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agspo">GSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Qwen Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. GSPO exponentiates the mean log ratio; the exact sequence ratio exponentiates the sum, multiplying token ratios. Averaging changes length scaling and the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeated small shifts accumulate in a product but the geometric mean measures typical shift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18071">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d23ce2ac81343580">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gspo" data-paper-title="GSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e9419f1e0394ebb6">Should GSPO clip per token or per response?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agspo">GSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Qwen Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clip one ratio per response, shared across tokens. Mask padding from length. Candidate experiments do not reproduce real token rollouts, MoE routes or clusters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clipping each token and averaging usually differs from averaging then clipping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18071">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e9419f1e0394ebb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlcr" data-paper-title="Beyond Binary Rewards: Training LMs to Reason About Their Uncertainty" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rlcr-9a05e032" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ac0af70774f8783">Why predict both an answer and confidence in RLCR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlcr">Beyond Binary Rewards: Training LMs to Reason About Their Uncertainty</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correctness-only reward does not incentivize honest probabilities. A proper score evaluates probability and outcome, rewarding truthful probabilities in expectation under its assumptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model that often errs should report moderate confidence instead of certainty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2507.16806-rlcr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ac0af70774f8783">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlcr" data-paper-title="Beyond Binary Rewards: Training LMs to Reason About Their Uncertainty" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e491a49ab4ec08e3">Why need proper scoring in addition to correctness rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlcr">Beyond Binary Rewards: Training LMs to Reason About Their Uncertainty</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Binary reward cannot distinguish justified caution from false certainty. Proper scoring couples probabilities with outcomes to incentivize honesty. Report accuracy and calibration separately; local Brier gradients aren&#x27;t full RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A quiz bot claiming certainty on unfamiliar items can be penalized for that confidence even when ordinary rewards ignore it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2507.16806-rlcr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e491a49ab4ec08e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlcr" data-paper-title="Beyond Binary Rewards: Training LMs to Reason About Their Uncertainty" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf73ac1980f7fa4e">How does RLCR differ from displaying confidence after training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlcr">Beyond Binary Rewards: Training LMs to Reason About Their Uncertainty</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A displayed field needn&#x27;t affect optimization; RLCR incorporates a scoring rule. Local Brier/hybrid objectives are mechanism evidence, not full rollouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 90% badge doesn&#x27;t mean bad calibration was penalized in training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2507.16806-rlcr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf73ac1980f7fa4e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlcr" data-paper-title="Beyond Binary Rewards: Training LMs to Reason About Their Uncertainty" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e79bc66d4f44aa7">Which classes receive local RLCR Brier gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlcr">Beyond Binary Rewards: Training LMs to Reason About Their Uncertainty</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute squared differences between the complete softmax distribution and one-hot target and backpropagate over all candidates, not just the displayed choice. Hybrid includes CE; no paper-checkpoint RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Unselected classes consume probability mass and contribute to scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2507.16806-rlcr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e79bc66d4f44aa7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cispo" data-paper-title="CISPO / MiniMax-M1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-cispo-73dd09ad" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ba75db1b56d9b580">Why clip importance weights in CISPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acispo">CISPO / MiniMax-M1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MiniMax</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bound magnitude while preserving advantage direction and learning, unlike PPO min-surrogate flat regions. Separate frozen weights from differentiable logp.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A capped positive weight can still reinforce through logp.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13585">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2506.13585-cispo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ba75db1b56d9b580">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cispo" data-paper-title="CISPO / MiniMax-M1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ce326a3ad19568a3">Why does CISPO retain gradients for some tokens PPO would clip flat?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acispo">CISPO / MiniMax-M1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MiniMax</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clipped weights scale log-probability gradients while retaining advantage direction. PPO&#x27;s minimum is flat in certain quadrants. Test gradients, not only values or clipped advantages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare negative-advantage token can still receive bounded suppression even if PPO is flat.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13585">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2506.13585-cispo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ce326a3ad19568a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cispo" data-paper-title="CISPO / MiniMax-M1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-45e7baa94a6c0de4">Why aren&#x27;t CISPO and PPO the same because both clip?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acispo">CISPO / MiniMax-M1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MiniMax</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>PPO takes the minimum of clipped and unclipped surrogates. CISPO multiplies logp and advantage by clipped weight. Backward and out-of-range behavior differ despite matching bounds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One boundary can stop gradients; the other preserves updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13585">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2506.13585-cispo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-45e7baa94a6c0de4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cispo" data-paper-title="CISPO / MiniMax-M1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0a45c23f226dd11a">What if CISPO differentiates directly through the clipped ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acispo">CISPO / MiniMax-M1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MiniMax</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extra weight derivatives change the policy-gradient objective. Keep rollout, weight construction and logp path separate. Local checks do not reproduce MiniMax training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Current action logp should supply gradient without duplicating it through the weight branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13585">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2506.13585-cispo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0a45c23f226dd11a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ttrl" data-paper-title="TTRL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ttrl-f1272098" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e13260c6de1f2d65">Where does TTRL get rewards on unlabeled test tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Attrl">TTRL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PRIME-RL author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sample several answers, use majority consensus as a pseudo-label, reward agreement and update online. No gold, but consensus can be wrong; evaluate separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeatedly guessing the same wrong number creates agreement, not truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2504.16084-ttrl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e13260c6de1f2d65">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ttrl" data-paper-title="TTRL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c6d9c41a8ac4de24">Why label TTRL as adaptation rather than fixed-model evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Attrl">TTRL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PRIME-RL author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Test inputs trigger sampling and immediate parameter updates, so the evaluated model changes. Report sampling/adaptation budgets and keep gold in independent scoring. Pseudo-label consensus can reinforce errors; unlabeled isn&#x27;t no learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sampling and updating before answering differs from one call to the original model even without gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2504.16084-ttrl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c6d9c41a8ac4de24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ttrl" data-paper-title="TTRL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-de29d2e53a75bceb">How does TTRL differ from majority-vote inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Attrl">TTRL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PRIME-RL author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Voting just aggregates outputs; TTRL updates parameters using pseudo-rewards and affects later behavior. Account for training compute and persistent state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After the same samples, voting returns; TTRL additionally optimizes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2504.16084-ttrl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de29d2e53a75bceb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ttrl" data-paper-title="TTRL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-764787173229e3b9">May TTRL answer normalization see test gold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Attrl">TTRL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PRIME-RL author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Equivalence and votes must use permitted output rules; gold is scored afterward. Local loops aren&#x27;t paper-scale real rollouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not filter by the correct number before claiming an autonomous vote.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2504.16084-ttrl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-764787173229e3b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:luffy" data-paper-title="LUFFY" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-luffy-8fd3aff1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c299f856a9e50d38">Why combine offline demonstrations and online exploration in LUFFY?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aluffy">LUFFY</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Demonstrations reveal paths students rarely sample; online rollouts preserve current exploration. Handle shared support and source probabilities rather than pure imitation or narrow exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Experts show a proof while the student still generates attempts and receives feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14945">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2504.14945-luffy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c299f856a9e50d38">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:luffy" data-paper-title="LUFFY" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e37406dcb0a268f">Why track behavior μ in mixed demonstration/rollout batches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aluffy">LUFFY</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared batch doesn&#x27;t make sources on-policy. Importance ratios and regularization address source shift while keeping exploration. Students must still reach uncovered states; do not leak demos into evaluated inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Record expert success separately from failed student rollouts, not as a student sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14945">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2504.14945-luffy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e37406dcb0a268f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:luffy" data-paper-title="LUFFY" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e45f299abee943ba">How does LUFFY differ from inserting demonstrations into an ordinary GRPO group?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aluffy">LUFFY</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>External demonstrations have another sampling source and need correction/regularization. Treating them as student samples gives wrong denominator. Source-aware updates are more than adding good text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An inserted expert solution is not a lucky current-policy sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14945">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2504.14945-luffy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e45f299abee943ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:luffy" data-paper-title="LUFFY" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d4452a51f7d0b3b">What roles do μ and ref have in LUFFY?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aluffy">LUFFY</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>μ describes mixture sampling; ref anchors KL. Track online vs demonstration provenance. Local candidates aren&#x27;t paper text/distributed training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Expert data and initial-student reference need not have the same probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14945">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2504.14945-luffy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d4452a51f7d0b3b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:vapo" data-paper-title="VAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-vapo-b94393ac" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8e6b5956ce7b7a3c">Why emphasize a critic for long reasoning in VAPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avapo">VAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse terminal rewards leave prefixes without direct feedback; a critic supplies a baseline. Bias can grow with length, motivating pretrained value and length adaptation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Estimate later returns before an intermediate reasoning step gets terminal reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05118">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2504.05118-vapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8e6b5956ce7b7a3c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:vapo" data-paper-title="VAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0e539b78de945446">Why repair critic quality and adapt GAE to length instead of dropping the critic?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avapo">VAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse rewards and varying horizons amplify value error. VAPO pretrains the critic and adapts advantage estimation and actor to length. It doesn&#x27;t remove value learning, and local proxy lengths aren&#x27;t long-CoT evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Short and long solutions receive reward at different delays, so one estimator can have different bias/variance across them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05118">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2504.05118-vapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0e539b78de945446">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:vapo" data-paper-title="VAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d806ff9fba95bf37">What does VAPO trade for critic-free GRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avapo">VAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>GRPO uses same-prompt relative rewards without a critic. VAPO trains a critic for prefix values. Their costs and error sources differ; fewer models isn&#x27;t higher capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An all-wrong group has no relative signal while a critic can still estimate, possibly incorrectly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05118">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2504.05118-vapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d806ff9fba95bf37">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:vapo" data-paper-title="VAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f259ddc6b3c4d6b">Why isn&#x27;t the local VAPO critic a reproduced pretrained value model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avapo">VAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidate actions and proxy lengths simulate value–length coupling, not real long prefixes. Retain response-dependent GAE λ rather than claiming a fixed λ is equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A table of candidate values isn&#x27;t a neural critic reading thousands of reasoning tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05118">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2504.05118-vapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f259ddc6b3c4d6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dr-grpo" data-paper-title="Dr. GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-dr-grpo-c17c40d0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-aad7fc2a0748abfc">Why audit both response-length averaging and group standard deviation in Dr. GRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adr-grpo">Dr. GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · SAIL 研究团队</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They change weights by length and problem difficulty, not just numerical stability. Remove both while retaining group mean centering so reward differences preserve their scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal reward gaps get different magnitudes after normalization when group variances differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aad7fc2a0748abfc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dr-grpo" data-paper-title="Dr. GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-72916d57d18ee4c3">Why remove both group SD and within-response averaging?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adr-grpo">Dr. GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · SAIL 研究团队</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SD reweights difficulty groups by their local variation; token averaging changes long-versus-short contribution. Keep centered rewards and fixed aggregation, not remove all normalization or promise universal gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tiny group SD can amplify a comparable reward gap; response length adds another weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72916d57d18ee4c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dr-grpo" data-paper-title="Dr. GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b75da045562bf37a">Does Dr. GRPO still center group rewards like GRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adr-grpo">Dr. GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · SAIL 研究团队</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Subtract same-prompt mean, but omit the specified length and SD normalization. Dropping SD does not remove the baseline, and adding a global SD would change the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Judge each reply relative to group mean without dividing by group variation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b75da045562bf37a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dr-grpo" data-paper-title="Dr. GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ba362a618993555">Can proxy lengths establish removal of long-CoT length bias?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adr-grpo">Dr. GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · SAIL 研究团队</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A candidate policy has no generated length distribution. Proxy lengths expose normalization differences, not real token losses or long responses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing a simulated length doesn&#x27;t produce early stopping behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ba362a618993555">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dapo" data-paper-title="DAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-dapo-b7495c1f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-22a113575bc73943">Why dynamically skip all-correct and all-wrong DAPO groups?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adapo">DAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Binary rewards without variance give no relative advantage and waste batch slots. Sample groups with distinctions; this doesn&#x27;t solve exploration on every difficult problem.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four failures give no ordering, so resample rather than repeatedly train on zeros.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14476">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2503.14476-dapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22a113575bc73943">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dapo" data-paper-title="DAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ebd8d3555febbac3">Why drop all-correct groups in Dynamic Sampling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adapo">DAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Centering equal all-correct/all-wrong rewards yields no relative direction, not worthless replies. Resample differentiable groups; Clip-Higher, token aggregation and length shaping handle other effects. Never select questions on test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A mixed-success group provides group-relative learning absent from an equal-reward group.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14476">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2503.14476-dapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ebd8d3555febbac3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dapo" data-paper-title="DAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1eb83514170cabf">Which side does DAPO Clip-Higher relax?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adapo">DAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raise the upper bound to retain room for beneficial probability increases; lower bound remains separate. Dynamic sampling, token loss and overlength shaping are also defining pieces.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Easier increase of a useful action needn&#x27;t loosen downward changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14476">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2503.14476-dapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1eb83514170cabf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dapo" data-paper-title="DAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f25cd80adbf410cf">How does DAPO token-level normalization differ from per-response averages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adapo">DAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sum over valid response tokens, then normalize together. Per-response means weight lengths differently. Also preserve dynamic filtering and overlength penalty. Proxy lengths don&#x27;t reproduce real masks or 32B training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Averaging a short and long reply separately is not averaging every token together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14476">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2503.14476-dapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f25cd80adbf410cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:reinforce-plus" data-paper-title="REINFORCE++" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-reinforce-plus-c6bb06c9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c36afea4bd44747">Why avoid each prompt&#x27;s SD in REINFORCE++?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Areinforce-plus">REINFORCE++</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researchers</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Few samples make local variance noisy and can overamplify some difficulty groups. Keep group centering and use a global scale without a critic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An accidentally tiny variance should not give one prompt excessive weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03262">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2501.03262-reinforce-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c36afea4bd44747">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:reinforce-plus" data-paper-title="REINFORCE++" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-939c465a1c7db3eb">Why center locally but scale globally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Areinforce-plus">REINFORCE++</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researchers</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Group mean removes common difficulty; local SD may amplify incidental low variance. Cross-batch scale makes units consistent without critic. Window and distribution matter; small EMA tests don&#x27;t prove stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two similarly separated groups shouldn&#x27;t receive very different weights just because one has tiny variance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03262">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2501.03262-reinforce-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-939c465a1c7db3eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:reinforce-plus" data-paper-title="REINFORCE++" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ecef13818d1e0f7e">Why isn&#x27;t global EMA normalization a reordering of GRPO normalization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Areinforce-plus">REINFORCE++</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researchers</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Statistics use different domains. Group means compare same-prompt samples; global second moments share scale. This changes cross-problem weighting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Groups with the same gap but different variances differ under local division, not a shared scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03262">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2501.03262-reinforce-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ecef13818d1e0f7e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:reinforce-plus" data-paper-title="REINFORCE++" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a8daf8a6d85b0f7">Can REINFORCE++ reestimate EMA from evaluation gold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Areinforce-plus">REINFORCE++</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researchers</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Maintain training state in batch order; test answers cannot tune scale. Small-candidate EMA validates semantics, not the large-batch distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scanning all test rewards to set the denominator leaks evaluation information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03262">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2501.03262-reinforce-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a8daf8a6d85b0f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rloo" data-paper-title="RLOO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rloo-064c4d91" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4b9c6d8a40ab7e4f">Why does RLOO treat a full response as one action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arloo">RLOO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cohere For AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal RLHF rewards suit response-level REINFORCE and avoid prefix values. Other same-prompt samples form a variance-reducing baseline; multiple samples are still needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A summary&#x27;s terminal score weights its complete logp relative to peers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14740">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2402.14740-rloo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4b9c6d8a40ab7e4f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rloo" data-paper-title="RLOO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f08c5af1cc0c720">Why exclude the current response from RLOO&#x27;s same-prompt baseline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arloo">RLOO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cohere For AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Peers provide an independent reference, not the current action&#x27;s random reward. Treating a response as one action avoids a value network but still requires enough samples, consistent rewards and any specified reference/evaluator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For reply one of four, average the other three so the baseline doesn&#x27;t move with its own reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14740">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2402.14740-rloo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f08c5af1cc0c720">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rloo" data-paper-title="RLOO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7349629a82265af6">How does leave-one-out differ from a mean including the current sample?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arloo">RLOO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cohere For AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>LOO excludes the sample&#x27;s own reward from its baseline. Including it changes dependency and scaling. Both are critic-free, but group size matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With two replies, the first&#x27;s LOO baseline is the second, not both averaged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14740">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2402.14740-rloo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7349629a82265af6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rloo" data-paper-title="RLOO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-593dd7b298e4697f">Can RLOO use the same formula at K=1?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arloo">RLOO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cohere For AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. K−1 is zero and there are no peers. Require sufficient group size and KL-shaped returns as appropriate. Local K=4 candidates aren&#x27;t 7B generation and real RM.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Zero-filling an empty baseline changes the estimator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
