</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo" data-paper-title="DeepSeekMath / GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-grpo-679757d4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1014e27ef04ab41">Why can GRPO omit a policy-sized value model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo">DeepSeekMath / GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same-prompt group mean and SD estimate relative advantages instead of a learned prefix value. Save critic resources but require repeated rollouts and differing feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Better attempts receive positive advantage relative to peers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03300">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1014e27ef04ab41">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo" data-paper-title="DeepSeekMath / GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-62e639b015b8e33e">How does GRPO obtain advantages without critic, and what are old and reference for?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo">DeepSeekMath / GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Center and scale group rewards for relative signal. Old gives sampling probabilities for ratio/clipping; reference anchors KL. Equal rewards provide no contrast. Candidate updates don&#x27;t reproduce full math training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A reference change alters regularization, not the historical rollout source.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03300">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62e639b015b8e33e">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo" data-paper-title="DeepSeekMath / GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5af499f3d629e3b1">Why are GRPO old and reference policies different roles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo">DeepSeekMath / GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Old supplies rollout and proximal ratios, reference anchors long-term KL. Old can refresh each batch independently of the reference; mixing couples update limits and regularization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fresh sampling updates old policy, not necessarily initial reference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo" data-paper-title="DeepSeekMath / GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">

<h2 id="qa-ad9a955723733b8a">What should GRPO do with equal group rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo">DeepSeekMath / GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Centered advantages are zero and SD needs protection; never invent differences using evaluator gold. Local six-action candidates aren&#x27;t DeepSeekMath generation.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:remax" data-paper-title="ReMax" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-87b16e785b3b5268">Why use same-prompt greedy reward as ReMax baseline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aremax">ReMax</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 香港中文大学（深圳）/ 深圳市大数据研究院</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It gives a prompt-specific reference without training value. Reinforce samples above greedy and suppress below it; greedy need not be correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sampled explanation better than the usual first choice gives positive credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:remax" data-paper-title="ReMax" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">

<h2 id="qa-4c70be2bb992c727">Must the ReMax greedy baseline be correct?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aremax">ReMax</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 香港中文大学（深圳）/ 深圳市大数据研究院</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is a variance-reducing comparator for the same prompt. Relative returns can be positive or negative independent of absolute correctness; baseline isn&#x27;t gold. Both paths still cost generation and scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A wrong greedy and correct sample yield positive signal; two wrong replies do not make greedy the standard answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:remax" data-paper-title="ReMax" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">

<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aremax">ReMax</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 香港中文大学（深圳）/ 深圳市大数据研究院</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ReMax additionally executes greedy decoding. RLOO uses other randomized responses. Both save the critic but spend generation differently and have different baseline errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare one greedy rollout&#x27;s cost to multiple peer samples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:remax" data-paper-title="ReMax" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">

<h2 id="qa-6fba78bf3d20b0b6">Should ReMax differentiate through greedy baseline reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aremax">ReMax</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 香港中文大学（深圳）/ 深圳市大数据研究院</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Treat it as fixed return, not a gradient through discrete decoding or scoring. Use the same prompt/protocol for both. Local greedy candidates do not establish memory or latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not invent an argmax reward gradient while updating the sampled policy.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ppo-rlhf" data-paper-title="InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">

<h2 id="qa-5003585127af1af3">Why distinguish reward model, critic, old policy and reference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Appo-rlhf">InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reward model scores preferences, critic predicts returns for advantages, old policy records sampling, and reference anchors SFT drift. Shared initialization doesn&#x27;t merge roles. Candidate updates aren&#x27;t human ranking, reward-model training or large-scale RLHF.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A reward model rates a reply, a critic forecasts its return, and reference measures deviation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2203.02155-ppo-rlhf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5003585127af1af3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ppo-rlhf" data-paper-title="InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">

<h2 id="qa-eaf08fcf780ae999">Why distinguish PPO clipping from reference KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Appo-rlhf">InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clipping limits a proximal step relative to old policy; KL anchors drift relative to a reference over longer horizons. They aren&#x27;t substitutes and don&#x27;t prevent reward exploitation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeated small steps can still travel far from the initial policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2203.02155-ppo-rlhf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eaf08fcf780ae999">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ppo-rlhf" data-paper-title="InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f6c88f5229999b2">Does local PPO-RLHF include a learned reward model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Appo-rlhf">InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

Which quantities must remain distinct across online sampling, old-policy probabilities, and current-policy updates?

## Takeaway

RL post-training collects trajectories and rewards, then computes advantages and an update objective. GRPO uses relative rewards for a group of answers to one prompt instead of a separate critic. DAPO changes clipping, uninformative groups, and length handling. Asynchrony, off-policy replay, and inference/training engine differences change the sampling distribution. Old, current, and reference policies play different roles; their probabilities are not interchangeable.

## Example

For rewards 0, 0, 1, 1 on four answers, within-group advantages give a direction. If all four fail and get the same reward, group centering cannot distinguish them. Replaying cached trajectories does not freeze current probabilities, so do not blindly reuse old advantages and density ratios. Check whether importance weights are required and which sampler they refer to.

## Common pitfall

Stability and capability require separate evidence. Finite gradients, clipping tests, and ratio checks do not prove better reasoning. Low offline loss cannot replace actual rollout comparisons. Full checkpoint and long-trajectory runs retain the cost and GPU gates; a runnable formula is not finished training.

## Reading order

Start with GRPO sampling, advantages, ratios, and reference KL. Then read DAPO for zero-variance groups and training stability, and TIS for probability conventions across the sampling and training engines.

1. [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03300)
2. [DAPO](../../../../post-training/2503.14476-dapo/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14476)
3. [TIS](../../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en.md) · [Original source](https://fengyao.notion.site/off-policy-rl)

## Check your understanding

If every answer in a group has the same reward, can a larger batch or repeated calculation of the same advantages create a new direction?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    Not from the same centered rewards. Check whether reward is too coarse, tasks are too easy or hard, or resampling or another legitimate signal would help. Do not read test answers to manufacture nonzero advantages. Recheck the objective and budget after any change.
